name: Tent
overview: Scripture reveals that tents served as essential dwellings for key patriarchs such as Noah, Abraham, and Lot, providing both shelter and a place for worship, as seen when Abraham pitched his tent and built altars to the LORD (Genesis 12:8; 13:18). Tents also symbolized a nomadic lifestyle connected to shepherding and cattle-raising, exemplified by Jabal, described as the father of those who dwell in tents and keep livestock (Genesis 4:20). The tent was not only a practical home but a setting for divine encounters, demonstrated by the LORD appearing to Abraham at the tent door (Genesis 18:1), and it functioned as a private space, as indicated by Noah being uncovered within his tent (Genesis 9:21).
